content:
maya (Platform): Canary alarm: 5xx rate jumped to 3% on route model-serv after we pushed canary at 5% traffic. Seeing tail latency spikes too. @jen are you oncall?
jen (Oncall): oncall here. saw alerts, looking at traces now.
deploy-bot: Canary r-20260320-81 deployed -> traffic split: 95/5. Health checks: 97% passing.
sam (Eng): quick thought — prefer fast rollback to 0% and then do a controlled re-deploy. We should also check KV prefix compatibility; last time cache mismatches caused stale embeddings.
oliver (SRE): +1 for fast rollback. But if we abruptly cut traffic we might leave stale sessions with new kv keys. Need a KV resync plan or a prefix fallback.
lee (ML infra): What if we flip traffic to the previous variant and enable a short redirect-backoff in the router so existing sessions can finish? Example command: `ri rollout set-traffic --id r-20260320-81 --split 100:0 --grace 30s`
maya (Platform): That looks good. Concrete plan proposal: 1) set traffic 100%->stable, 2) enable safemode for canary group to reject new sessions, 3) run kv-resync for affected prefixes, 4) monitor telemetry for 10m, then re-deploy fix or unfreeze. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
jen (Oncall): I can run traffic flip now. Will also trigger `kv:resync` after flip.
sam (Eng): For kv-resync, prefer incremental resync to avoid thundering herd: `kv resync --prefix embeddings/model-serv --batch 2000 --rate-limit 500/s`
oliver (SRE): Add a small TTL bump plan: older keys keep TTL for 5m to let sessions finish. `kv update-ttl --prefix embeddings/model-serv --delta +300s`
maya (Platform): console UX note: we keep hitting this manual checklist. Would be nice to have a rollback action that atomically flips traffic + runs a chosen kv operation (resync/clear/ttl-bump) and toggles safemode. Filing a follow-up feature ticket.
sam (Eng): Agree. Also add telemetry tags during rollback so we can filter the dashboards by rollback-run-id.
jen (Oncall): executing step 1: `ri rollout set-traffic --id r-20260320-81 --split 100:0`
deploy-bot: Traffic flip scheduled -> running. 30s grace applied.
juniper (notified): (automated trace job) linking traces to rollback-run-id rb-3421
jen (Oncall): flip completed. Observability shows 5xx drop to baseline. Starting kv resync now with incremental batches.
sam (Eng): Will watch per-route latency dashboards. If anything >2x p95 for more than 3 min we pause resync.
lee (ML infra): small note: resync job will create new keys with current schema; check compatibility for older stable.
oliver (SRE): Good catch. I'm enabling an on-the-fly fallback map so routers can translate new -> old keys until TTL expires. `router config apply --map resync-fallback`
maya (Platform): All right — sounds like we're coordinated. Postmortem follow-ups: console rollback + kv-operation button, automatic rollback-run tagging in telemetry, and docs for TTL/resync playbook.
jen (Oncall): resync finished. No regressions seen in the next 10m. Closing incident but leaving rollback-run flagged for audit. :white_check_mark:
sam (Eng): One small action item: add an optional `--resync-strategy=incremental|flush|ttl-bump` flag to the CLI and expose in console.
maya (Platform): noted. I'll create the ticket and link to this thread. Thanks all! :pray:
